extracted.subtask_description: A collection of Associated Press newswire items covering international politics, military doctrine, legal rulings, and administrative recommendations; written for general news consumers and editors. The page is a historical/archival compilation of short dispatches rather than a single long feature.

rubrics_metrics.name: UNESCO director selection criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: The person chosen for UNESCO education director must move to Paris and meet 'pretty stiff requirements' spelled out for the job.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stated required attributes include high professional standing and familiarity with foreign affairs as well as with how to deal with international bodies. Practical notes in text: the job carries a tax-free salary; a deadline (Nov. 1) for candidates was mentioned; selection likely favors candidates comfortable relocating and working at the international (Paris) headquarters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Planned Mobilization Register participation guidelines
rubrics_metrics.description: Manufacturers listed in the Register of Planned Mobilization Production should ensure their register entries are meaningful and up-to-date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommendations include purging dead-head entries, keeping plant surveys and mobilization schedules current, determining whether production potential would qualify a plant for wartime production, identifying and listing likely military customers, and treating potential military customers the same as any other customer (i.e., documenting intent to sell). The Register links manufacturers to military procurement planners, so accurate listings matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Refugee Relief Act asylum eligibility (as applied in reported ruling)
rubrics_metrics.description: Judge Goodman indicated the Refugee Relief Act can apply to 'any alien of good moral character' in his country when certain conditions exist.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Context in the report: Immigration authorities had refused asylum to two former trainees on grounds they were members of an armed force of a U.S.-allied nation; the judge remanded the case to the Attorney General to investigate the men's character and report to Congress. Practical implications: asylum eligibility under the Act requires assessment of the individual's moral character and other statutory disqualifiers (e.g., membership in certain armed forces), and courts may order administrative fact-finding before final resolution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Immigration/remand procedural guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: When asylum/refugee claims raise questions about an applicant's character or status, a judge may remand the case to administrative authorities for investigation and report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The reported case shows the judge remanded to the Attorney General to investigate character and report to Congress, indicating a procedure where judicial review can require fact-finding by immigration authorities prior to final determination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Army command and firepower doctrine for ground operations
rubrics_metrics.description: New Army doctrine advocates that the ground commander must have direct and unchallenged command and the fire power and authority to direct it against any target that might affect the outcome, even at long ranges.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Doctrine stresses giving ground commanders the authority to employ long-range firepower (including atomic-tipped ballistic missiles in planning) and to extend their firepower via new missile systems. It also notes interservice disputes over control of long-range weapons (Army vs. Air Force). Emphasis is on centralizing command and ensuring the commander has means to affect distant targets relevant to the battle outcome.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limited-war weapons selection and conduct principles
rubrics_metrics.description: In limited war, forces should avoid automatic escalation to widescale retaliation; instead choose weapons carefully, place them accurately on forces directly engaged, and cease their application as soon as the aggression ends.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quoted guidance (Air Force/Quarles) emphasizes maintaining retaliatory preparedness while distinguishing limited engagements from all-out war. Principles include: do not react automatically to limited aggression with broad strikes; select proportional weapons; target forces directly engaged; stop operations when aggression ends to prevent escalation; and recognize that use of atomic weapons is not a guarantee against further escalation.
